evidence.ai_role: Gradient-boosted decision trees learn baseline features predicting a later eGFR-category label.
evidence.tested: Patient-level 80/20 split; fold-refitted preprocessing/feature selection and development-only 10-fold model selection; reserved internal test.
evidence.unknown: Single-centre retrospective inclusion depends on follow-up availability; post hoc threshold and medication scenarios are exploratory, not treatment effects.

source_review.scope: Primary full manuscript Methods, Results, validation protocol and limitations independently reviewed.

summary: A preprint evaluated baseline clinical prediction of six-month eGFR-category worsening in 2,022 adults with diabetes and renal dysfunction. CatBoost was selected within development data and reached AUROC 0.91 in a reserved 405-patient internal test set. Inputs were restricted to baseline and pre-index records. A post hoc top 5% prioritization rule identified19 of48 test-set events, missing more than half. Category worsening did not require 90-day persistence, so this is not confirmed chronic progression. The single-centre retrospective study establishes no external clinical utility or causal benefit from medication exposure.
title: CatBoost estimates six-month kidney-function category decline retrospectively
